candidates.title: Train action chunk boundaries rather than maximizing chunk length
candidates.rule: For text-based long-horizon agents, compare trajectory-derived chunk-boundary supervision and chunk-aware credit with simply permitting multiple primitive actions per decision.
candidates.passage: Removing either component degrades both task success and decision efficiency.
candidates.finding: On ALFWorld with Llama-3.1-8B, full Space reaches 94.5% unseen success versus 88.3% without skills and 89.1% without chunk-aware advantages. Plain multi-action GRPO can collapse to single actions or overlong chunks depending on the model.
candidates.conditions: Skills supply temporal boundaries during training; inference emits primitive chunks without the skill library.
candidates.limitations: Text environments and successful training trajectories constrain transfer. Reduced observation frequency can be risky in stochastic settings. Fewer LLM rounds do not automatically mean equal total token cost or safe execution.
candidates.validation_test: Compare one-action, unrestricted multi-action and boundary-supervised policies under measured spend; score task success, replanning delays and failures when state changes midway through a chunk.
